title: He hid it under the tent.
paragraphs: He hid it under the tent.
And a whole nation paid for one man’s secret.

Israel had just seen walls fall at Jericho by the power of God. Victory was fresh. Faith was high. But when they went up against little Ai, they were crushed. Men died. Courage melted. Joshua fell on his face wondering why heaven felt silent. The answer was not weak strategy. It was hidden sin. Achan took what God had forbidden, buried it beneath his camp, and thought nobody would know (Joshua 7:1, 10–12).
That is the terror of secret sin.

Achan’s hands touched stolen treasure, but the wound spread through the whole community. That is how sin works. We call it private. God calls it poison. We bury it under comfort, excuses, image, reputation. But what is hidden in the tent will eventually show up on the battlefield.

The deepest tragedy of Achan’s story is not gold. Not Babylonian garments. It is this: he traded the presence of God for something he could not keep. He reached for what glittered and lost what mattered. And many of us still do the same. We gamble peace for pleasure. Calling for compromise. Conviction for a moment of craving.

Yet the story does not end as a warning only. It points us to our need for a better rescue. Because if all hidden sin deserves judgment, then who can stand? Only this: Jesus Christ bore the judgment our sin deserves. He is the true substitute for the guilty. On the cross, He took our shame out from under the tent and brought it into the light. Not to destroy the repentant, but to cleanse them. Not to crush the broken, but to redeem them. “If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness” (1 John 1:9).
So do not protect what is killing you.

Confess it. Kill it by grace. Run to Christ. The God who exposed sin in Joshua 7 is the same God who offers mercy through the blood of His Son. There is no victory for a people who hide from God. But there is healing, restoration, and renewed strength for those who repent before Him.
